segments.name: GA4 user suspecting undercounted traffic
segments.organization: Any business or site owner running GA4 behind a cookie/consent banner (SaaS marketing sites, e-commerce, content publishers)
segments.workflow: Operates a cookie-consent banner (CMP) in front of GA4; checks GA4 session/pageview totals against ad spend, server logs or business volume and finds a gap after tightening consent settings.
segments.need: An independent, consent-independent pageview count to measure and validate the size of the GA4 consent gap, run side-by-side with GA4.
segments.buyer_role: Marketing lead, growth/analytics owner, or site owner who reads GA4 reports
segments.user_role: Same person who reads GA4 dashboards
segments.current_alternative: Google Analytics 4 with a consent banner/CMP (e.g. Cookiebot, OneTrust), accepting the undercount as unavoidable

counterevidence_summary: An expert SEO source frames GA4's native Consent Mode, not a second analytics platform, as the recommended long-term fix for this exact problem. — Recommends staying within the GA4 ecosystem via Consent Mode rather than adopting an independent measurement tool, directly undermining the premise that this audience's remedy of choice is a second, consent-independent product. Review before prioritising.

The documented diagnostic workflow for the GA4 gap used SEO tools, not a parallel analytics platform. — Shows the agency's actual remedy relied on existing SEO tools rather than adopting a second analytics platform, suggesting the documented workflow does not naturally lead to this product category even though it does not rule it out. Minor condition; does not exclude this audience.

The forum discussion of this exact pain ended without any solution, including no mention of an independent analytics tool. — Indicates the discussion remained open and unresolved, with no participant suggesting a second, consent-independent analytics tool as the fix. Minor condition; does not exclude this audience.
reasons: The Shopify Community thread and the Mad Fish Digital case study both document the hypothesized pain directly: GA4 undercounts or misattributes traffic once a cookie consent banner is active, creating a measurable gap against known business/sales volume.

Product truth capabilities (no cookies/trackers/consent required; narrow, non-personal EU-processed data scope; no DPA required) are compatible with running a consent-independent pageview count alongside GA4.

None of the three fetched sources mention Simple Analytics or any 'run a second analytics tool alongside GA4' workflow; the documented remedies are GA4 Consent Mode, Enhanced Conversions, server-side tagging, or cross-checking with SEO tools, not a second analytics platform.

The Shopify Community forum is a concrete, named public venue where a real site owner ('cdem') posted this exact GA4-consent-gap complaint, giving a verifiable instance of the audience and a venue to reach similar posters.
Re-ranked on matching researched sources (2 fetched).
unknowns: Whether this audience, when actually fixing the problem, would choose a parallel independent tool over GA4-native fixes (Consent Mode, Enhanced Conversions) that the corpus shows being recommended first.
No first-person account in the corpus of anyone evaluating or adopting Simple Analytics specifically for this purpose.
Population size and the typical buyer role (marketing lead vs. store owner vs. agency) for this exact pain beyond the handful of documented cases.
No verified venue or example establishes findability yet.
Review the counterevidence before prioritising this audience.

evidence.quote: This is the best long term solution.

evidence.quote: enable enhanced conversions, which means you send customer data to Google, and based on AI, will Google fill in the gap

segments.who: Marketing/growth owners and site operators running GA4 with a consent banner who suspect undercounted traffic
segments.why_them: They have an observable, named trigger (a sudden or ongoing GA4 drop after a consent banner change) and a stated want (an independent count), which Simple Analytics' free 30-day GA4 comparison directly targets.
segments.trigger: GA4 totals look unexpectedly low versus known business volume, especially right after adding or tightening a consent banner.
pains: GA4 may undercount traffic when visitors reject consent or are blocked (inferred)
Uncertainty about how big the consent gap actually is without a second, independent measurement
segments.objection: GA4's advanced consent mode might already model most of the missing visitors, so some buyers won't see the need for a second tool.
segments.basis: Multiple independent SEO/agency blog posts (gitconnected, Mad Fish Digital, taggurus.co.uk) describe specific, large GA4 session drops attributed to consent banners; Simple Analytics' Enterprise free 30-day GA4 comparison and compliance FAQ page are built around this exact comparison workflow.
